scope: Conditional marginal-Gaussian quadratic check of qualified native-corrected supernova fits. No new background or CMB evaluations, empirical error rescaling or physical age correction.
smooth_basis: Four natural-cubic-spline coefficients, with the z=0 coefficient fixed to zero; same basis and extrapolation as ReleasedDistances.
replicate_distribution: At fixed physical and sampled nuisance parameters, r_rep is Gaussian with Sigma=C+sigma^2 B B^T; project only the one free global magnitude. The replicated quadratic is chi-square with N-1 degrees of freedom.
flat_magnitude_measure: Density accounting uses the same improper flat global-magnitude measure as ReleasedDistances. This is not a proper normalization over the full data space or an absolute evidence normalization.
smooth_replication_interpretation: A new B coefficient vector is drawn from its declared prior for each entire replicated dataset. This is mixed replication, not prediction of the same universe or hosts conditioned on a shared inferred luminosity curve.
tails: For every stored observed quadratic Q, compute Pr(Q_rep<=Q) and Pr(Q_rep>=Q) under chi-square(N-1), then average using the original untrimmed native/proposal posterior weights. No fitted cosmological-parameter subtraction and no additional subtraction for properly integrated Gaussian modes.
limitations: The posterior uses the same observations as the discrepancy. Tail averages are posterior-predictive diagnostics, not calibrated frequentist p-values, evidence, covariance validation, raw-flux or host-age tests. The released Gaussian distance covariance, selection corrections, classification treatment, sample selection and probe assumptions remain conditional. An aggregate quadratic can hide redshift-dependent, population-dependent, correlated or directional failures. Floating-point zero tail values are not exclusion bounds.
